hints: Look at what is being made in this reaction, stable combustion products like $\text{CO}_2$ and $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ usually tell you a lot about heat change.
Recall that forming very stable compounds from elements releases a lot of energy, which is why their $\Delta H_f^\ominus$ values are large and negative.
Check whether each reason describes energy being released or absorbed, bond breaking takes in energy while bond making and forming stable products gives out energy.
walkthrough:
**Spot the type of reaction**

Think of this like burning a fuel fragment. You start with $\text{CH}_3$ and $\text{NO}_2$ and you finish with $\text{N}_2$, $\text{CO}_2$ and $\text{H}_2\text{O}$.

$$4\text{CH}_3 + 7\text{NO}_2 \rightarrow 3\tfrac{1}{2}\text{N}_2 + 4\text{CO}_2 + 6\text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Decide exothermic or endothermic**

Making the very stable products $\text{CO}_2$ and $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ releases a lot of heat. Reactions that make these combustion products are almost always exothermic.

**Link to enthalpy of formation**

The standard enthalpy of formation is the energy change when 1 mole of a compound forms from its elements.

$$\Delta H_r^\ominus = \sum \Delta H_f^\ominus(\text{products}) - \sum \Delta H_f^\ominus(\text{reactants})$$

**Choose the correct reason**

Both $\text{CO}_2$ and $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ have large negative $\Delta H_f^\ominus$ values. That means a lot of energy is given out when they form, so the overall reaction is exothermic.

options.A: Incorrect. Converting chemical energy to heat energy describes an exothermic change, not an endothermic one. This reaction gives out heat to form stable products.
options.B: Incorrect on both parts. The reaction is exothermic, not endothermic. Also, the very strong $\text{N}\equiv\text{N}$ bond is formed in the products, so making it releases energy rather than absorbing it.
options.C: Correct. The reaction is exothermic because it produces very stable $\text{CO}_2$ and $\text{H}_2\text{O}$, both of which have negative $\Delta H_f^\ominus$ values showing that their formation releases energy.
options.D: Incorrect reason. Although the reaction is exothermic, breaking double bonds in $\text{NO}_2$ requires energy input (endothermic step). It cannot explain why the overall reaction gives out energy, the energy release comes from forming new strong bonds in $\text{CO}_2$, $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ and $\text{N}_2$.
